strings.name: Reinhold Messner
strings.summary: From Dolomite rock climbing, Messner became a central figure in high-altitude mountaineering. With Peter Habeler he first climbed Everest without supplemental oxygen, later returning solo. Lightweight climbing, his fourteen-peak project and polar exploration shaped the field; later summit-location reassessments disputed some older records. He also served in the European Parliament and developed mountain museums, continuing to write and advocate the cultural value of wild mountains.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: His high-altitude breakthroughs changed oxygen-free and lightweight climbing practices, with international influence on exploration.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Raised in a German-speaking family in South Tyrol, Italy.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Everest without supplemental oxygen
strings.highlights.h1.text: Completed the historic ascent with Habeler in 1978.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Learned climbing in the Dolomites as a child, studied engineering and briefly worked as a teacher.
strings.highlights.h2.title: From exploration to storytelling
strings.highlights.h2.text: Uses museums, books and films to transmit climbing experience and mountain culture.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Publishes Lebenszeit
strings.timeline.t1.text: Coauthored with Diane Messner on aging, loss and the value of a finite life.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Mountain museum development
strings.timeline.t2.text: Firmian became a major center of the Messner Mountain Museum system.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Elected to European Parliament
strings.timeline.t3.text: Served with Italy's Green political movement until 2004.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Fourteen-peak milestone
strings.timeline.t4.text: Completed the then-recognized fourteen eight-thousanders; later topographic reviews disputed some summit records.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Solo Everest ascent
strings.timeline.t5.text: Climbed Everest's north side alone without supplemental oxygen.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Oxygen-free Everest ascent
strings.timeline.t6.text: Summited with Peter Habeler, changing perceptions of high-altitude human limits.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Nanga Parbat turning point
strings.timeline.t7.text: Summited with brother Günther, who died on descent; Messner suffered severe frostbite.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Technical Alpine climbs
strings.timeline.t8.text: First ascents including Heiligkreuzkofel's middle pillar established his European climbing reputation.
